title: Illinois Shines Solar Incentive 2026-27: What You Are Paid per Credit
desc: Illinois Shines pays for the solar renewable energy credits your home system creates: $70.37 or $80.77 per credit for small systems in 2026-27, plus a $20 adder for customer-owned systems.
lead: Illinois does not hand you a solar rebate check. Instead, a state program called Illinois Shines pays for the renewable energy credits your panels create, and your installer passes the value to you. A credit is one megawatt-hour of solar power. For a small home system in the 2026-27 program year, the price per credit is $70.37 or $80.77, depending on where you live. We read the prices on October 6, 2026.
cards_heading: What Illinois Shines pays for a home system
cards_intro: The payment is the credit price multiplied by the credits your system is expected to make over its 15 or 20 year contract. A bigger system makes more credits, and so earns more.

cards.title: Home system 10 kW or smaller
cards.note: $70.37 in Group A, which is the Ameren Illinois and MidAmerican area. $80.77 in Group B, which is the ComEd area. A system of 10 to 25 kW pays $60.92 in Group A and $79.21 in Group B.

cards.title: Customer-owned adder
cards.note: Extra $20 per credit if you own the system (not a lease or power purchase agreement) and do not claim a federal credit. This runs through the 2026-27 year.

cards.title: Illinois Solar for All
cards.note: A separate state program for income-eligible households, with required bill savings and little or no cost up front. The site lists no dollar amount.

after_cards: Illinois Shines pays each year's price to the installer or vendor you sign with. It is that company that must pass the value on to you, and its contract should say how.
sections: For contracts approved on or after June 1, 2026, Illinois Shines pays 50 percent of the credit value when your system is switched on, and the rest in equal parts over the next six years. The old schedule paid everything at once. Your vendor may pay you in a lump sum, in parts, or fold it into your price. Read the disclosure form your vendor must give you. It now has a field that asks the vendor to explain how any promised payment is passed on.

We cannot give you your payment, because it depends on what your roof will produce. The state expects the system's output when it approves the project. As a simple illustration, 10 credits at $80.77 would be $807.70, and the $20 adder would add $200. That is only arithmetic to show how the price works. Ask your vendor for the number of credits in your contract.

The state splits Illinois into two groups. Group A covers the service areas of Ameren Illinois, MidAmerican, Mt. Carmel Public Utility, and electric cooperatives and city utilities in the MISO grid region. Group B covers ComEd and cooperatives and city utilities in the PJM grid region. We read this in the 2025-26 program guidebook, since the 2026-27 guidebook was not read. Naperville has its own city electric company, so ask which group applies to your address before you sign.

The federal tax credit for home solar ended for spending after December 31, 2025. That is why Illinois added the $20 adder for customer-owned systems. The adder only applies if you do not take a federal credit, which is no longer possible for a new system, so confirm with your vendor how the contract handles it.

We did not read the current Illinois net metering rules for 2026, so we do not state how much your utility pays for extra power. Ask your vendor to show you the bill credit rules in writing and to model your yearly savings with them.
claim_steps: Find out whether you are in Ameren Illinois's area (Group A) or ComEd's area (Group B) by looking at your electric bill.
Ask for quotes only from Illinois Shines Approved Vendors. Illinois Solar for All has its own vendor list for lower-income homes.
Ask each vendor how many credits your contract will have and how it will pass the money to you.
Let the vendor submit the application and handle the paperwork with the utility.
Keep the contract, the disclosure form and the energization date.
faq: Not exactly. It buys the renewable energy credits your system makes, and your vendor passes the value on to you. How and when you are paid is in your contract.
That depends on how much power your roof will make. The price is $70.37 or $80.77 per credit for systems of 10 kW or less in 2026-27, plus $20 per credit if you own the system.
Group A covers the Ameren Illinois and MidAmerican areas. Group B covers the ComEd area.
Is the federal solar credit still available?
No. It ended for spending after December 31, 2025.
Can I lease my system and still get the incentive?
The $20 customer-owned adder does not apply to a lease or power purchase agreement. Ask your vendor whether a lease is offered and how the incentive is passed on.
